text:
Anchor model: comments anchor to text via two literal substrings (start, end), each of which must occur exactly once in the post body. Ambiguous or missing anchors error rather than disambiguate.

Rejected alternatives during design (user explicitly weighed and dismissed):
- Occurrence-index anchors (quote + Nth-match): fragile when text is paraphrased between rounds.
- Stable-hash anchors over surrounding context: more code, no real win for a tool that's used live.
- Line/character offsets in the post-frontmatter source: fragile across edits.

The user picked strict-match-or-error precisely because LLMs sometimes paraphrase quotes; loud failure pushes them to re-quote rather than silently misanchoring. If a future change reintroduces fuzzy matching, this is the reason to push back.

graphe is intentionally minimalist for ephemeral review sessions. The user explicitly excluded these and would push back if proposed:

- Multiple posts / directory browsing (single file per invocation).
- Static HTML output (live server only).
- Authentication, multi-user, or remote hosting.
- Comment author field, resolved/unresolved state, threading, replies (delete instead of resolve; comments are ephemeral and disappear when no longer relevant).
- History of past comments.
- Math rendering (KaTeX).
- Mobile layout polish (Tufte assumes wide screens; just don't crash narrow).

If any of these come up as 'wouldn't it be nice', the answer is no unless the user changes their mind.
